How the project came together

Five stages, from siting the borehole to lifting water to a steel tank.

Every GWK borehole starts underground, before any equipment reaches site. The sequence below is what carried this project from a site visit to a working water point.

  1. 01
    Hydrogeological survey
    Ground investigation to identify a viable drilling point and estimate depth to water, using geophysical resistivity readings taken across the site.
  2. 02
    WRA permit application
    Survey findings submitted to the Water Resources Authority to secure authorization to abstract groundwater at the site, ahead of any drilling.
  3. 03
    Drilling
    The rig sunk the borehole to 80 metres, with casing installed to secure the well and protect it from collapse.
  4. 04
    Electric pump installation
    A submersible electric pump was set at working depth and connected, ready to deliver water to the surface on demand.
  5. 05
    Steel tower and tank erection
    A galvanized steel tower was assembled on site and fitted with a pressed-steel tank, giving the supply enough elevation for gravity-fed distribution.

The completed installation

Elevated tank, commissioned and ready to supply.

The finished structure stands beside the borehole, drawing water from 80 metres below ground and holding it at height for gravity-fed supply across the site. Below is the view from the roadside.
